Priyom — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick follow-up from our side: 

- Compliance: FinPay is in-scope for PCI and we need to make sure any shared infrastructure does not increase our compliance scope. We prefer dedicated capacity if isolation can be demonstrated (VLANs, separate GPU pools, customer-level logging).
- Performance targets: our engineering goal is p99 <= 500ms for ~256-token responses during normal peak patterns; we can tolerate brief spikes but want guarantees around long tail degradation.
- Noisy neighbor concern: our security team is worried about co-tenant load causing tail latency or unpredictable throttling.

Can Marissa or someone confirm: for Dedicated, are we talking about physical GPU isolation (dedicated hosts/pools) or logical isolation on shared nodes? How do you measure and guarantee SLOs (p95/p99), and what telemetry/logs would we get for audits? Also include what fallback options exist (e.g., auto-burst to additional dedicated capacity or routing to a hosted variant) during incidents.

If you can send a short summary of the isolation boundaries and the SLOs you can commit to, we can get Legal involved. Proposed deep-dive times look fine — Tue 11/3 10 PT would work.

Hi Samir — thanks for outlining the requirements. I wanted to capture the technical approach and what we can offer from a Dedicated capacity perspective so you have something concrete for Legal/infra to review. Short version: Dedicated = strong isolation + observable SLOs; we can support a gated PoC to validate. Details below.

What "Dedicated" means operationally:
- Dedicated GPU pools: you get reserved GPU capacity in a pool that is not shared with other Redwood customers. That means no co-tenant model on those hosts.
- Network isolation: VPC peering + dedicated subnets; option for customer-managed NAT / egress controls to keep PCI scope tight.
- Storage/Logs: per-customer logging buckets and audit trails. We can provide the log schema and examples for audits.

SLOs and measurement:
- Baseline performance: for common open LLMs and 256-token requests, our internal baseline for a 1-GPU serving slice is: p50 ~ 80–120ms, p95 ~ 180–300ms, p99 ~ 450–650ms depending on model and sequence length.
- Dedicated SLA option: we can contract p95 and p99 windows for your dedicated pool tailored to the chosen model. Example contractual target we can offer for PoC: p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 600ms (measured over 5-minute windows, with allowance for maintenance windows defined in the SLA).
- Telemetry: we provide token-level timing breakdowns, per-request traces, and percentile dashboards. For audits we can export raw request logs (anonymized as required) and synthetic run results.

Handling noisy-neighbor / capacity incidents:
- Because pools are physically dedicated, noisy-neighbor risk from external tenants is eliminated. Within the pool, we control scheduling and can enforce QoS to prevent one customer workload from starving others.
- Autoscaling & burst: we can configure reserved baseline capacity + burst buffer (private burst or managed overflow). For critical windows we can pre-provision an additional GPU and rotate traffic.
- Fallback policies: automatic traffic routing to a warmed hosted variant (same model family with slightly different perf/cost profile) is available if your pool hits capacity limits; we can make that a controlled, monitored fallback with alerting.

Proposed PoC plan (30 days):
1) Provision a 2-GPU dedicated pool (model X-small, to be chosen).
2) Run your synthetic traffic during agreed peak windows; we will run parallel synthetic load to validate headroom.
3) Weekly telemetry review and one final performance report you can share with Legal/compliance.
4) Sign a short MSA addendum that defines the SLO targets and incident playbook for the PoC period.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_SLA_v1.pdf (SLA draft for Dedicated pools) — this contains proposed definitions for maintenance windows, measurement methodology, and remedies. Also attached SOC2 evidence summary.

If this sounds good I can prepare a brief technical appendix for Legal and draft the PoC MSA addendum. Priyom — can you confirm commercial terms we discussed (30-day reduced rate for PoC, then commit or cancel)? Vivek — can you prepare the benchmark runbook?
